summary.headline: Texmaco Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR753 crore but PAT rose 85.9% YoY to INR52 crore; order book INR9,923 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was INR753 crore, hit by lower freight car and Rail & Green execution, while Bright Power electrical revenue grew 76.8% YoY to INR175 crore. EBITDA was INR81 crore (10.8% margin), flat YoY, and PAT rose 85.9% YoY to INR52 crore (6.9% margin) on lower finance costs. Management said the order book stood at INR9,923 crore at June 30, 2026, with private and export orders at 96.4% of freight car orders in Q1 FY27. Strategic updates covered the leasing JV with Trinity (Texmaco stake to fall from 50% to 34%), the Wabtec air brake JV, a South Africa order of about INR4,100 crore, and a 2030 vision of doubling the top line.

segments.name: Freight Cars (FCD)
segments.commentary: 1,054 freight cars delivered in Q1 FY27; execution lower on supply-chain stress tied to oil and gas prices. Private and export share of orders rose from 21% in FY25 to 79% in FY26 and 96.4% in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Rail Infra & Green (formerly Kalindee)
segments.commentary: Revenue lower YoY; EBIT margin turned positive at 1.4% versus an EBIT loss in Q1 FY26.

segments.name: Bright Power (Electrical infra)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR175 crore, +76.8% YoY; EBIT margin 10.8%, up 150 bps YoY.

segments.name: Foundry
segments.commentary: Production of 5,148 tonnes in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Core business EBITDA margin target of 1.2% to 3% over the next 1 to 3 years (as stated by management; the figure is ambiguous in the transcript).
Vision 2030: core rolling stock revenue of INR5,000-6,000 crore; aim to double the top line to about 2x by 2030 with a steady bottom line in the mid-teens.
New businesses could add 20% to 50% top-line growth in some years; management would not give absolute FY27 or FY28 numbers.

South Africa order (about INR4,100 crore, wagons plus 15-year maintenance, which is 30-35% of value): about 50-60% expected to execute in FY28; locomotive value to be additional and not yet finalised.
Management expects freight car output and supply-chain normalisation to improve from coming quarters; no volume target given.
capex_capacity: Leasing: about 35 rakes operating today; near-term readiness to invest in about 100 more rakes. Leasing JV with Trinity: Texmaco stake falls from 50% to 34%; capital allocation to be modest in percentage terms.
Capacity described as elastic (15,000-16,000 commodity wagons possible), but management is prioritising specialised wagons over volume.
South Africa: considering a locomotive plant and a wagon manufacturing plant; management declined to confirm the INR200-300 crore reported investment figure.
Wheelset supply from Rail Wheel Factory: enough stock for current export and private orders.
demand_pricing: Order book INR9,923 crore at June 30, 2026, with more than 6,000 wagons in hand (per CFO).
Q1 FY27 order wins include about INR5,200 crore, of which the South Africa order is about INR4,100 crore; some export orders are under execution.
Management expects no Indian Railways wagon tender near term; it expects orders to come from private and export customers.
Other expenses rose because export freight charges are booked there while the related income is in revenue (CFO).

qa_highlights.question: Wagon leasing: is the report of about INR1,800 crore investment for about 100 rakes over 3-5 years correct?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm figures; it said the leasing JV is separate from Texmaco, with Trinity entry cutting Texmaco's stake to 34%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the South Africa order exposure correct: a locomotive and wagon plant costing INR200-300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not confirm the numbers; it said it is open to facilities for localisation and that footprint matters more than investment amount.

qa_highlights.question: Execution timeline for the INR5,200 crore order and the maintenance share?
qa_highlights.answer: The South Africa order is about INR4,100 crore, not INR5,200 crore, and is executable mainly in FY28; maintenance is 15 years and about 30-35% of value.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue and EBITDA guidance for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No absolute guidance; management pointed to a core EBITDA margin target of 1.2% to 3% and possible 20-50% top-line growth from new businesses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did freight car output fall, and is there a 2030 roadmap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed oil and gas-driven supply-chain stress and said order book is healthy; it reiterated Vision 2030 (2x top line, mid-teens bottom line).

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook as the mix moves to private and export orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin is hard to predict and that it expects to sustain and improve margins, without giving a number.

risks_watch: Supply-chain stress from high oil and gas prices and supplier dependence; management says output should improve from coming quarters.
Dependence on the South Africa order, which is lumpy and where the locomotive component is not yet finalised or partnered.
No Indian Railways wagon tender yet; management says it is insulated for now.
Leasing and new-business capital needs, and the reduced JV stake after the Trinity entry.
Freight car volumes fell YoY; watch Q2 deliveries and whether the margin gain holds as execution resumes.
Management declined to give FY27 and FY28 revenue or margin numbers; a call for clearer guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and the order mix, and expansive on the strategic vision. Evasive on numbers: it declined to confirm reported investment figures, locomotive values and absolute FY27 or FY28 targets, and it repeatedly deferred to future announcements.
key_quotes: So, this order is executable in the next financial year.
We want to have at least a 50% share in terms of the business from a jump from 15% to 50%.
The share of private sector and export orders increased from 21% in FY25 to 79% in FY26 and further to 96.4% in Q1 FY27.

Turnaround from EBIT loss in Q1 FY26

adds.what: Leasing fleet: about 100 more rakes readiness to invest (about 35 rakes operating today)

growth.why: Management guides to 2x top line by 2030 and a 20-50% growth option from new businesses, with 15-20% analyst framing; backing is the INR9,923 crore order book (incl. INR4,100 crore South Africa order, ~50% executing in FY28) and leasing rakes, but no FY27 absolute numbers were given, so support is partial.
